reason: The cited articles (9, 13, 15, 26(5)) collectively establish the regulatory basis for testing accuracy, hallucination, repeatability, and limits. Article 9 sets the general obligation for high-risk AI systems to be accurate. Article 13 requires conformity assessments, which would include testing for these metrics. Article 15 mandates post-market monitoring, which would involve reviewing performance and failure cases. Article 26(5) provides for the European AI Board to issue guidelines on testing methodologies, further supporting the control objective.
applicability_note: This control is applicable to all AI systems, as the EU AI Act imposes obligations on providers of high-risk systems and requires transparency for other systems, both of which necessitate performance evaluation.
challenge_comment: The challenge lies in defining and applying appropriate benchmarks and thresholds for diverse AI systems, as the regulation provides a framework but not specific technical standards for every use case.
